findings.description: The old summarize() fetched each distinct sensor's calibration once and cached it in a dict. The new code calls calibrated() for every reading, and calibrated() calls source.load(), so a batch with N readings from a few sensors now runs N SQL queries instead of one per sensor. With large batches this becomes an N+1 query pattern.
findings.suggestion: Cache calibrations per sensor_id within summarize(), for example with a local dict, and pass the cached Calibration into the per-reading logic.
findings.title: Calibration loaded from the database once per reading instead of once per sensor

findings.description: The reason always reads '{rejected} readings out of range'. When the zone has too high a rejected share, it also reports the raw rejected count without the total. The message is not wrong, but a zone with mean None and rejected 0 cannot occur, so this is minor. The message does not say that the zone was flagged because the rejected share exceeded the threshold.
findings.suggestion: Include the rejected share or total count in the message, e.g. f"{summary.rejected}/{summary.count + summary.rejected} readings out of range".
findings.title: Misleading 'inspect' reason when the zone was rejected for another cause
